research_question: Does model-based semantic compression of the same first Lean diagnostic improve early valid proposals and early score improvement compared with exact structured_v1 extraction?
independent_variable: Compile-error details policy only: deterministic structured_v1 caps (S) versus independent model message summarization and verbatim goal/context selection (M), from the same extracted first diagnostic.

S.description: Exact prior structured_v1 extraction and deterministic per-field caps, unchanged.

M.description: One fresh independent summarizer job receives uncapped first diagnostic extraction, summarizes message, retains verbatim goal substring and ordered whole context lines, and emits the same complete JSON schema.

schedule: Prespecified counterbalanced dispatch order; rolling queue maximum 2 fresh solvers, no paired model seed claim.
primary_outcome: Per problem/condition, number of runs whose best cost at proposal 3 is strictly below the original cost of 1.
secondary_outcomes: Valid proposal count among first 3 per run
First valid proposal and first score improvement (not achieved by 10 recorded as censored/null)
Best observed local cost at proposals 3,6,10
Compile failures and timeouts; final validation and record replay
Compile-error feedback exposure count, same-error offline formatter check, and first-error preservation
Next-proposal validity after a compile failure, descriptive only due to endogenous trajectories
Number of summarizer jobs, input/output sizes, elapsed time and schema/substring compliance; fallback incidents
Extracted and delivered goal/context character retention; whole-goal preservation where feasible
constants: Exact naive prompt, original statement/source/context and pinned libraries per problem
Same frozen original denominator and ranking, 10 proposals including rejections
Normal compilation plus 3 fresh measurement runs, final revalidation, 420-second limit per invocation
Same worker code; feedback condition not disclosed in initial request; independent fresh solver per trial
Same source access restrictions and best/latest history; no extra Lean calls, library search, repairs, strategy hints or additional budget
Successful feedback, response rejection and non-compile failures retain exact legacy behavior
Only the same first diagnostic is given to the summarizer: no proof source, full compiler log, problem statement, history or repair strategies.
M uses one independent model summarizer per compile failure, no automatic retry; invalid or missing summary falls back to exact S and records an incident.
readiness_policy: One fresh original normal+3 validation and imports-only check per problem before any solver dispatch, with two problems checked concurrently. Full shared-runtime SHA256 before and after.
limitations: Two fresh independent runs per condition are exploratory, not a significance test.
Exact backend model ID, sampling seed, hidden context, internal model calls and cost unobservable.
S and M receive the same extraction; M adds a model transformation and variable latency, so this does not isolate compression alone.
Both problems have already informed development; not held-out generalization.
Libraries are shared read-only by policy; no OS-level isolation.
Offline old-log formatter checks are manipulation checks, not extra solver trials or performance evidence.
Strategy-free semantic fidelity cannot be proved by deterministic schema/substring checks; preserve raw inputs and outputs for review.
Summarizer jobs are observable; exact internal model-call count, backend model ID and monetary cost remain unknown for both roles.

summary_policy.input: uncapped prior _extract output (including its existing last-12-local-context restriction)
summary_policy.invalid_or_missing_output: exact structured_v1 fallback and recorded incident
summary_policy.local_context: whole original lines in original order; ordered subsequence
summary_policy.whole_goal_feasibility: canonical envelope with empty message/context and truncated=true plus 200 characters <=1600
